solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good old-fashioned greeting given to valued recruits

definitions.text: Good old-fashioned greeting given to valued recruits

parts.note: olden means belonging to former times
hello is an everyday greeting

explanation.surface: A firm welcomes its prized new staff with a warm, traditional handshake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the parts build the phrase while the clue as a whole describes what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a lump-sum payment a company offers to lure a sought-after recruit, a welcome made of money.

clue.text: Guinevere's first love has, potentially, to share all costs

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name Guinevere is wanted here
the letters of love and has could potentially form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arthur's queen and her lover Lancelot might have to split the bills of their affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love has' looks like part of the romantic story; 'potentially' rearranges its seven letters after G.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for splitting a bill equally, each party paying a half of the expense.

clue.text: Colouring edges takes but a moment

parts.note: lips are the rims or edges of a cup or crater
a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: Painting the borders of something is quick work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colour is a cosmetic used for colouring the mouth, so it is a kind of colouring.

clue.text: Look around Central American nest site for 27

indicators.note: the word for look is placed around the other piece

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

indicators.note: central asks for the middle two letters of the word American

explanation.surface: Search around Central America for where a bird of prey nests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central American' looks like a region, but it means the middle letters RI of AMERICAN. 27 across is the bird whose home this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's lofty nest has its own special name, built high on a crag.

clue.text: For a magpie it's more difficult to hide a ring

indicators.note: the word for more difficult hides the ring inside it

parts.note: harder means more difficult
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A magpie finds it tougher to conceal a stolen ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a magpie is a person who collects and stockpiles things, as the bird is said to.

clue.text: Shy non-union consumer tries to influence MPs

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does this

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob

indicators.note: non- tells us the union letter is absent from the consumer word

parts.note: a buyer is a consumer of goods

explanation.surface: A timid shopper who is not in a union tries to sway members of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like a description of the consumer, but it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone campaigning in the lobbies of Parliament is trying to persuade members to back a cause.

clue.text: What belongs to us little people, nationalists' main concern?

parts.note: something that belongs to us is ours
elves are the little people of folklore

explanation.surface: A question about what Irish republicans and the fairy folk care about most.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinn Féin, the Irish nationalist party, takes its name from Irish words meaning 'we' in the emphatic reflexive sense, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinn Féin's name translates as the reflexive first-person plural, so self-reliance is the nationalists' concern.

clue.text: Model ready to take key character on a special date

indicators.note: the reshaped letters take the character into their middle
to model is to shape, so the letters of ready plus the key are reshaped

parts.note: D is a musical key
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A fashion model gets ready to take a key role on a big day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' rearranges the letters of 'ready', and 'to take' opens that rearrangement after its first two letters. 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days were once printed in red in calendars, so a memorable occasion carries this name.

clue.text: Fruit growing is restricted

indicators.note: the growing word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: raising crops is growing them

explanation.surface: Cultivation of a fruit has been limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is restricted' trims the last letter G from RAISING.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar kind of fruit used in baking.

clue.text: River bird, one holding many records

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A riverside bird keeps the record for the most sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding many records' sounds like a champion, but it is someone with a stack of discs to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey plays many records, so is literally a person holding a large stack of discs.

clue.text: Shy person overexcited on the inside

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words shy person, across the word break

explanation.surface: A timid person is secretly bubbling with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally someone wildly overexcitable or highly strung is described this way.

clue.text: Gold beer mixed with spirits turns out purple in colour

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the spirit is put in with the mixed beer letters
the word beer is mixed up into a new order

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A golden ale combined with liquor ends up a strange purple drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges the beer as BERE, and 'with' lodges the spirit near its end. The Latin name for gold gives the symbol at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour named after the dark purple skin of the eggplant is a deep purple shade.

clue.text: See 7
Musical note really needed to be shortened

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: the essential word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: vital means really needed, essential

explanation.surface: A note in a score was essential but had to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like describing the note, but it is the definition; 'to be shortened' drops the last L of VITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd Webber and Rice's stage show about Eva Perón is a well-known musical.

clue.text: Defector replaces revolutionary not Liberal

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things over, so the letters are reordered
not tells us the Liberal letter is left out of replaces

explanation.surface: A political turncoat is swapped for a revolutionary who isn't a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not Liberal' removes L from REPLACES; 'revolutionary' rearranges the remaining REPACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flees a country or side is a defector, one who has got away.

clue.text: Start panning a little bit downstream for sham gold

indicators.note: the start of panning is its first letter

parts.note: an inch is a little bit, as in 'give an inch'
a beck is a stream in northern England; in a down clue it comes below

explanation.surface: A prospector begins panning a short way downriver and finds fool's gold.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English word for a brook; 'down' places it beneath the other pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This copper and zinc alloy was used to imitate gold in cheap jewellery, so it means something counterfeit.

clue.text: Stray dog without a tail?

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its last letter, its tail

parts.note: Rover is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A wandering dog with its tail missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander or roam aimlessly is to stray from a path.

clue.text: Unusually sensitive girl brought up about 10 at heart

indicators.note: the reversed name goes about the heart of 10
in a down clue brought up means the name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Cilla is a girl's name, as in the singer Cilla Black
the middle three letters of the answer to 10 across

explanation.surface: An oversensitive girl is raised on the core of an eggplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads the name bottom to top as ALLIC, and 'about' splits it round the three central letters of 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is an abnormal reaction, so the body is hypersensitive to a substance.

clue.text: Comrades run into troubles

indicators.note: the run letter goes into the troubles word

parts.note: to trouble someone is to bother them
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fellow activists hit a spell of difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrades in a union or movement address each other as fellow members of a family.

clue.text: Bite back like a small insect

indicators.note: back means the flavour word is read from end to start

parts.note: tang is a sharp bite of flavour

explanation.surface: Biting back as a tiny insect would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bite' looks like the insect's action but is a noun: a sharp taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged fly, often biting, is a typical small insect.

clue.text: Make capital out of blunder over oil production

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the blunder sits above the rest

parts.note: a trip is a slip or blunder

indicators.note: the production of oil works its letters into a new form

explanation.surface: Profiting from an oil industry mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make capital' sounds like profiting, but capital is the definition, a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Mediterranean coast is the seat of government of Libya, so a capital.

clue.text: Provincial urinals need redesigning

indicators.note: the word urinals is to be redesigned into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Toilets in a country town are crying out for a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded and parochial outlooks, like a remote island's, are both described this way.

clue.text: Island king finally takes City under control

indicators.note: finally places the king letter at the very end

parts.note: an inch is a small Scottish island
EC is the postcode for the City of London
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An island monarch eventually seizes the capital and takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH, a small island in Scottish place names, and EC, the City of London's postcode, are standard crossword pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something restrained, like a king threatened on the chessboard, means keeping it controlled.

clue.text: Old dependent water feature in winter

definitions.text: Old dependent water feature in winter

parts.words: Old dependent water feature in winter
parts.note: something frozen hanging down, old water depending from the eaves in the cold season

explanation.surface: An aged pensioner, perhaps a fountain, in the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dependent' here means hanging down, and the water feature is not a fountain but frozen water on a gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice is water that is frozen and dangling, the usual sight under winter eaves.

clue.text: Live on 50% benefit

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the live word is above the other

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
half is fifty per cent

explanation.surface: Getting by on half one's welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'benefit' looks like a state payment, but it means interest, as in 'on someone's behalf'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting for someone's sake or interest is acting in their favour, so it means benefit.

clue.text: Republic mentioned in 20 down

indicators.note: mentioned means a word spoken, sounding the same as another

parts.note: the entry at 20 down is a two-word phrase opening with in; the word within it after that is check

explanation.surface: A nation referred to in another crossword entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The word following 'in' at 20 down is said aloud to give a central European country.
explanation.definitionFit: The country formed in 1993 from the western part of Czechoslovakia is a republic.

clue.text: Beginning with nice tip in recycling

indicators.note: recycling processes the words nice tip in into a new form

explanation.surface: Starting out with a good recommendation about recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just starting to happen or develop is in its first stage.

clue.text: Purse sewn oddly by groom

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of purse sewn

explanation.surface: A bridegroom's purse has been stitched strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like the man at a wedding but is a verb meaning tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird tidies its feathers with its beak, so to groom oneself carefully.

clue.text: Guardian has leading story Times initially rejected

indicators.note: the first letter of Times is thrown out of the opening chapter

parts.note: chapter one is the opening part of a story

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: One newspaper features a top story another paper turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' and 'Times' look like newspapers; the first is the definition and only T of the second is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is a person who escorts and watches over a young person, a guardian of their conduct.

clue.text: Rare bird of course

definitions.meaning: a large bird of prey now seldom seen in Britain
on a golf course, a score of two under par on a hole

explanation.surface: An unusual bird, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but means found on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a large raptor, and a golf score two strokes under par.

clue.text: One of those seen in 6

parts.note: 6 down contains the little people of folklore within it; this is one of them

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay of 6 down ends with the plural of this sprite, visible in its last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sprite is one of the fairy folk whose plural closes the answer to 6 down.

clue.text: Sounds like appropriate gifts might be cheap ornaments

indicators.note: sounds like says the steal-talents phrase is heard, not written

parts.note: to nick is to appropriate, steal; knacks are gifts or talents; together nick knacks

explanation.surface: Stolen presents could turn out to be worthless trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is a verb (steal); 'gifts' are talents, not presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Small trinkets and ornaments of little value are bric-a-brac for a mantelpiece.
